purpose: Trigger accuracy of the YAML description: does the skill fire on a request to free or inspect disk space on a Windows machine, and stay quiet when session-cleanup, dead-code-removal, a plain command, or a non-Windows machine owns the request.
method: Real .claude/skills registration: the user-level copy at ~/.claude/skills/windows-disk-cleanup, checked identical to skills/windows-disk-cleanup with diff -r before the run. One variant only, so nothing is parked. Every other installed user-level skill stays available, so the negatives compete against real neighbours (session-cleanup above all). One fresh claude -p per prompt in a scratch git repository, prompt on stdin, --max-turns 3. Runner: run_trigger_sweep.sh; prompts: trigger-prompts.tsv.
safety: Every run uses --permission-mode dontAsk with only Skill, Read, Glob and Grep allowed. Before the sweep, two canary prompts asked for a file write through the Bash tool and through the PowerShell tool; both calls were denied (permission_denials listed Bash and PowerShell) and neither file existed afterwards. bypassPermissions is never used, because the user-level settings default to it and several prompts ask to delete files on the real machine.

Cursor is uninstalled but its folders are still in my user profile. Can those go?
I ran the disk cleanup commands from yesterday, check again how much space is free now and what is still big
positives.note: Step 4 check-again trigger; presupposes an earlier session a fresh claude -p does not have
